lane: G87-CSCT (Cover-Stratified Curvilinear Fault-Zone Tomography & Crack-Tip Dinkelbach Cover)
hypothesis: Cross-scale paired magnetic-gravity & LiDAR-DEM edge persistence stratified across basin-cover depth regimes (44 cover-stratified physical tomograms across USGS 3DEP 1 m LiDAR, 100 m DEM/chi, multi-depth upward-continued isostatic gravity, USGS GeoDAWN magnetics & K/Th/U metasomatism, MT crustal conductivity, and DOE GDR #1391 thermal springs/wells & geothermometers), fused with strictly fold-visible crack-tip & relay-ramp fracture mechanics via a Leave-One-Quadrant-Out LightGBM + HistGradientBoosting ensemble and emitted via exact CELF Dinkelbach 300 m Tversky submodular maximum coverage with lateral stress-shadow collar (d > 3.0 px, 37,654 binary dots).
mechanism: Normal faults in the Great Basin accumulate displacement across two regimes missed by single-layer scarp detectors: (1) range-front/piedmont splays, tip horsetails, and en-echelon relay ramps beyond mapped terminations (300 m - 3 km), where stress transfer concentrates slip along strike-aligned physical discontinuities; and (2) blind intrabasin faults buried under 50-1,500 m of Pleistocene lacustrine/alluvial fill where topographic scarps decay exponentially with relief (divisive background normalization) while upward-continued gravity steps, magnetic vertical-gradient edges, Th/K hydrothermal alteration ratios, and thermal fluid upflow persist at depth. Exact linear expectation of max_{u in S} K(|y - u|) eliminates kernel double-counting on short high-probability blobs while the 3.0-px lateral collar removes zero-credit digitization-halo false positives.
named_non_fault_mimic: Pleistocene Lake Lahontan (~1,330 m) and Lake Bonneville (~1,460-1,552 m) wave-cut paleoshoreline benches, alluvial fan-lobe risers, pre-Quaternary felsic-tuff/intrusive lithologic contacts (which create magnetic or Th/K steps without brittle fault offset), and partial LiDAR survey tile boundaries.
